leads.title: French Penal Code Article 225-1 as amended 18 November 2016
leads.documents: Prohibits discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation and gender identity; applicable in French Guiana as overseas department of France.
leads.detail: Cited in text as article 225-1 amended to replace 'sexual identity' with 'gender identity' on 18 November 2016; prior protections enacted 1985 (sexual orientation) and July 2012 (sexual identity). No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: French Labour Code (Code du travail) Chapter 2
leads.documents: Prohibits exclusion from recruitment, sanction, dismissal or discriminatory measures on account of sexual orientation and gender identity, among other grounds.
leads.detail: Quoted verbatim in Discrimination protections section. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change - Constitutional Council ruling 17 November 2016
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without sex reassignment surgery, sterilisation, or psychiatrist certificates; requires court application; effective 1 January 2017. Applies in French Guiana.
leads.detail: Cited as Senate approval 6 Nov 2015, Assembly approval 24 May 2016 and 12 July 2016 and 12 Oct, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published in Journal Officiel next day. No URL visible.

leads.title: B. vs France - European Court of Human Rights (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling that ended France's ban on legal gender change and required recognition for transgender people even after medical/surgical transition.
leads.detail: Cited as 'B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights' 1992 case. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe report on France (2022)
leads.documents: Documents significant issues with gender-affirming healthcare in France: lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location; recommends informed consent and self-determination model.
leads.detail: Cited as 'report published in 2022 by ILGA-Europe'. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: DILCRAH - French Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred
leads.documents: Documents France's institutional rights machinery against anti-LGBT hatred; 2022 controversy over president of scientific committee membership in The Little Mermaid Observatory.
leads.detail: Cited as DILCRAH with 2022 revelation and resignation/step-away. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 amending anti-discrimination legislation; Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881 Title 3 Articles 20 and 21
leads.documents: Makes homophobic/sexist/racist comments illegal (45,000 euro fine and/or 12 months imprisonment); creates Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité; increases penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation.
leads.detail: Cited as National Assembly approval 31 Dec 2004; first conviction Jan 2006 of Christian Vanneste later cancelled by Court of Cassation. No URL visible.

leads.title: Report released 16 May 2020 on homophobic and transphobic attacks (Ministry/Police figures)
leads.documents: Documents enforcement/incidents: ~1,870 victims of transphobic and homophobic attacks identified by police in 2019 (+36% vs ~1,380 in 2018), released before IDAHOTB.
leads.detail: Cited as report released 16 May 2020 right before International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia. No URL visible.

leads.title: Law legalising same-sex marriage (Law of 17-18 May 2013) - Constitutional Council decision 17 May 2013
leads.documents: Legalises same-sex marriage and joint adoption in all France including overseas departments/territories including French Guiana; first ceremony 29 May Montpellier.
leads.detail: Cited as Senate approval 12 April, Assembly 23 April, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 May 2013, signed by President Francois Hollande 18 May 2013, published in Journal Officiel next day; overseas vote detail: 1 deputy from French Guiana voted in favor, 1 abstained. No URL visible.

leads.title: Law banning conversion therapy (published 1 February 2022)
leads.documents: Legally bans conversion therapy with punishments of 2 years imprisonment and/or 30,000 euro fine; relevant to trans-visitor safety.
leads.detail: Cited as Senate passage 7 Dec 2020, National Assembly concurrence 25 Jan 2022, officially published 1 Feb 2022; proposal by MP Laurence Vanceunebrock-Mialon summer 2019. No URL visible.
